test_title: PYST 05: SSC Stenographer 2025: English Language & Comprehension (Held On: 07 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
In the following question, the first and the last parts of the sentence/passage are numbered 1 and 6. The rest of the sentence/passage is split into four parts-P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find the most logical order of the parts between 1 and 6.

The spacecraft initiated descent towards the red planet.

P: The data gathered during this process will aid future missions.

Q: The heat shield protected it from atmospheric entry.

R: Soon after, the parachutes deployed successfully.

S: Engineers monitored every second of the landing sequence.

6. This landing marked a historic step in interplanetary exploration.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
 
• The sentence begins with the spacecraft initiating its descent towards the red planet. 
 
• **Sentence Q comes first** as it explains how the spacecraft is protected during atmospheric entry: 
 
 
• "The heat shield protected it from atmospheric entry." 
 
 
 
• **Sentence S follows** because engineers monitoring the landing sequence logically comes next: 
 
 
• "Engineers monitored every second of the landing sequence." 
 
 
 
• **Sentence R is the third** as it describes the parachutes deploying successfully: 
 
 
• "Soon after, the parachutes deployed successfully." 
 
 
 
• **Sentence P concludes** as it highlights the importance of the data gathered during the landing process: 
 
 
• "The data gathered during this process will aid future missions." 
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **QSRP**. 

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"The spacecraft initiated descent towards the red planet. The heat shield protected it from atmospheric entry. Engineers monitored every second of the landing sequence. Soon after, the parachutes deployed successfully. The data gathered during this process will aid future missions. This landing marked a historic step in interplanetary exploration."
